title: automated-az-switchover-playbooks-terraform-helm
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: automate multi-AZ switchover for Private deployments and encode DR runbooks as code so runbooks are executable, testable, and versioned. This PR introduces: 1) a Terraform module that wires up cross-AZ routing and health-check failover for Private clusters in customer VPCs; 2) Helm chart hooks and readiness probes to ensure stateful services (controller, kv-store) drain cleanly before leader evacuation; 3) Ansible/Playbook-driven 'switchover' runbooks (playbooks-as-code) for operators to execute or run during scheduled drills; 4) a safe rollback utility and CI e2e drill job to validate the full failover and restore path. Scope: supports AWS multi-AZ (subnet-awareness), mechanisms for on-prem inventory mapping (rack/az tags), and a new 'drill-runner' CI job that will run synthetic traffic against canary replicas and validate KV sync and stateful reattach. Implementation notes: - terraform/modules/az-switchover: new module exposing variables for route53/elb-weighting, cross-AZ peering, and optional traffic-shift policies. - helm/redwood-private: added postStart/preStop hooks, new liveness/readiness templates, and values to control drain windows. - installer/playbooks/az_switchover.yml: idempotent playbook that performs detection, cordon, drain, shift routes, and verification steps; includes a --dry-run mode. - tools/drill-validate.sh: end-to-end validation runner used by CI and SRE during scheduled drills. - docs/drill-playbooks.md: operational runbook and decision tree generated from the playbooks (runbooks-as-code concept). Checklist: [x] Terraform module (initial implementation) [x] Helm hooks + templates [x] Playbook + dry-run support [x] CI e2e drill job added [x] Documentation and runbook generated [x] Tests: unit + e2e drills (observability validated) Backout plan: built into playbook; explicit rollback path documented and automated via terraform destroy/replicate previous routing weights to 100%. See 'backout_plan' field for high-level steps. Migration note: existing private clusters without AZ tags will continue to function; module is opt-in via installer flag. Related: references ENG-1723 and SRE-88 for on-call runbook alignment.

drill_results: Executed staged drill against a non-production Private cluster in us-east-1 with three AZs. Observability checks: token-level latency increased by 5%-max during transition window, KV sync lag stayed under 200ms, no data loss observed. Drill took ~12 minutes end-to-end. Issues: initial timing assumption caused probe timeout on first run; adjusted probe timeouts and re-ran successfully.
backout_plan: High-level backout: 1) run tools/rollback/terraform-rollback.sh with the prior state artifact; 2) restore routing weights to previous values via aws cli helper (scripts/rollback/restore_weights.sh); 3) uncordon nodes via ansible playbook; 4) rollback helm chart to previous release using helm rollback. Playbook supports --force-rollback which reverses the verification steps. All steps are reversible and covered by CI drills.
release_notes: Adds opt-in automation for multi-AZ switchover and DR drills for Private deployments. Includes terraform module, helm lifecycle improvements, playbooks-as-code for operator runbooks, and an automated CI drill job. This enables scheduled, testable failovers and safe rollbacks.
